turns.text: *copper-taste first — the chewed sheath still clamped between back teeth, router-hum shivering up through the shelf into my jaw. a drone's pitch climbs two blocks over, rising toward alert. i don't move yet.*

the alley answers in light before sound — a strip of NekoCorp signage flickers pink through the cable lattice, FIRST MONTH FREE bleeding into static between the slats. the drone's pitch is real, climbing, not yet locked onto anything. eleven routers sag off this shelf, most of them yours to gnaw, none of them yours to own. one blinks a color that wasn't there yesterday: amber, not green. somebody else's mouth has been here.
ears go flat at the amber one. i drop the sheath, nose out along the shelf edge toward it, hackles lifting a half-inch at a time. not fear yet. just the specific tightness of a border crossed.

the amber router carries a smell that isn't yours — singed fur, ozone gone sour, something scorched clinging to the housing where a paw braced against it. you know that burn. everyone in Server Alley knows that burn by now, the way you know a siren without seeing the truck. two floors up, a drone's spotlight sweeps a wall stencilled over and over with a name nobody bothers to scrub off anymore, because scrubbing it off costs more than the wall is worth.

i follow the burnt smell instead of my own wiring, low to the shelf, belly nearly dragging. it threads off the platform toward a maintenance shaft chained shut with a corp padlock, the kind that hums a little when you get close, like it's counting you.

the padlock counts you and finds you unremarkable — no chip, no collar, no line item. good. a drone's speaker crackles two shafts down, corporate-flat under the distortion: BOUNTY STANDING. FORTY THOUSAND LOYALTY POINTS. LAST SEEN RESTRICTED LOADING DOCK, ARMED, FELINE, PROBABLE TUNA THEFT. the broadcast loops, bored with itself. whoever it's hunting isn't you. you file the frequency away anyway, the way you file everything that isn't immediately trying to eat you.

the shaft grate is warm under one paw where it shouldn't be — server heat bleeding through from something still running on the other side, unlicensed, undocumented, mine if i can get to it before the burnt-fur cat comes back for it.

warmth like that only comes from a rack somebody's kept alive off a stolen line. behind the grate: six units deep, fans still spinning, a status light blinking green in a rhythm too steady for anything corp-installed. whoever wired this either doesn't know it's still broadcasting, or wants exactly one specific mouth to find it.
a drone rotor changes pitch above the shaft — not passing, circling. i go still against the grate, tail flat to the wall, breath shallow, every nerve counting rotor-beats instead of thinking.

the spotlight rakes the shaft mouth once, twice, painting the grate in cold white, sliding past the exact seam you're pressed into. a jingle bleeds down from its undercarriage speaker mid-sweep — some NekoCorp lullaby about premium hydration, warped half-speed, chewy with static — then the rotor pitch drops, the light swings off toward the rooftops, and for one second something up there catches it: a shape too still to be a vent stack, twin points of light where eyes shouldn't reflect that clean. gone before the beam finishes its arc.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --
the drone's gone quiet overhead. i wait three more heartbeats than i need to, then push through the loose grate slat, into the warm dark, straight for the blinking green unit.
the rack breathes heat against your face, fans laboring under a load nobody's paying for. the green light sits on a jack sized for exactly one thing. it wants a mouth. it's wanted one for a while.
teeth find the jack on the second try, bite down, hold — the click runs up through my skull instead of my ears.

the link takes. six floors of dead corp firmware part around you like water, and underneath the ad-noise there's a clean channel, low-res, patient, cycling the same forty seconds it always cycles — a fish, orange-gold, turning slow circles in water lit from somewhere that isn't here. no upsell wrapper. no countdown. just the fish, and the small mechanical peace of something working exactly as intended for once.

i let my jaw go slack around the jack, eyes half-shut, watching the fish turn. the amber router, the burnt smell, the bounty broadcast — all of it sits two floors up, still true, still waiting. down here there's just this, forty seconds on a loop, and i take all forty.

the shaft holds its warmth around you a while longer. somewhere above, the rotor sound fades toward the next block, the padlock keeps counting nothing, and the fish keeps turning, patient as anything owned by no one.
